title: Public RSS/Atom subscription feeds for publications and sections
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a reader, I want to subscribe to a publication or section using ordinary feed readers, so that I can follow published articles without visiting the site repeatedly.

Definition of Done for later implementation: standards-valid RSS and Atom publication/section feeds, stable item identity and canonical links, revision/withdrawal behavior, discoverability and published-only isolation covered by observable specifications. Depends on the shared published-content foundation. Examine existing Markus/static S3 publishing during implementation; avoid a parallel publisher. M8 PPY-f293ea mentions an optional feed: this epic owns the detailed subscription-feed behavior rather than duplicating M8's delivered latest/search JSON.

Deferred/YAGNI: Markdown+YAML exports, exact Contentful compatibility, extra export formats and authenticated draft previews. No feed endpoint, deployment or rollout is selected by this plan.

Approved post-save platform behavior: publish, saved published edits and unpublish automatically refresh both RSS and Atom alongside article/listings/indexes and sitemap. Both feed formats use the shared foundation selection and metadata rules. Ancillary failures must be visible/retryable; private draft saves never change public feed content. Detailed observable acceptance is in PPY-defff04e-17b5-4e28-9bb5-df412601a102. Implementation remains unstarted.

Feed eligibility is separately enforced and shared between RSS and Atom; existing public page/content identity, path placement, wiki navigation or include selection does not by itself make a page a feed entry. Static wiki/help and product pages do not automatically enter subscription feeds. Define eligible editorial types and other selection with the common published projection, preserving ordinary-page authoring and independent publication/access/draft gates. This does not add a separate wiki model or require every page to be a news item.

Organizing initiative: Markus for everything (PPY-23a743). This is one architecture with shared authored pages, includes/derived regeneration, published projection and delivery contracts. RSS/Atom and headless remain dependent on the shared foundation and post-save behavior. Incremental vertical slices are allowed as future planning, but a bespoke custom-Python composition shortcut contradicts the target design. Monitoring remains separate and linked, not a prerequisite. This architecture is now lower priority than the real Monitoring learning-loop slice; no implementation is authorized for it.

comments.text: Planning delivery: branch develop, direct Kanbus-only commit/push per AGENTS.md; GitHub reports develop unprotected, so no PR is required. Verified all 22 new records by kbs show: types, permitted parent links, descriptions, Gherkin, open/unassigned state, provenance and dependency targets. Both delivery epics depend on the common published-content foundation. Full-board kbs validate remains at the same 15 pre-existing abbreviated dependency-target errors; no new validation errors. No code/tests/dependencies/infrastructure/deployment changes; behavior implementation and executable acceptance remain unstarted.
